metadata.data_source: Synthetic CSV cohort generated with random seed 42.
metadata.circularity_note: Applications.csv shortlisting labels were partly generated from required-skill overlap and CGPA, which the matcher also uses, with about 17 percent of outcomes flipped. These matching metrics are partly circular.

matching_vs_shortlisting.precision_at_k_aggregation: macro average of per-job precision values; each per-job value uses min(k, applications for that job)

bootstrap_confidence_intervals.method: paired percentile bootstrap over application rows; same sampled indices for all methods

generator_shortlist_signal_ceiling.formula: base = 0.35 * required_skill_overlap + 0.025 * (cgpa - 7); noisy_signal = base + Gaussian(0, 0.32); preflip label = noisy_signal > 0.30; with probability 0.17 invert that label
generator_shortlist_signal_ceiling.source: ai/data/generate_data.py:76-78 (formula line 76, threshold line 77, flip line 78)
generator_shortlist_signal_ceiling.interpretation: The realized noisy generator score is an oracle ceiling: it contains the exact Gaussian draw used to create each label. It is not an available feature for a real candidate.

eligibility_gate_correctness.sampling: seeded simple random sample without replacement from the full student x job Cartesian product

jd_parser_accuracy.skill_scoring_unit: canonical skill occurrence per labelled JD; required/preferred distinction is also checked in field accuracy

risk_model.note: Evaluation uses a stratified 80/20 split with random_state=42; label 1 means no accepted offer.
caveats: About 73 percent of this cohort is unplaced, so accuracy near 0.77 is close to the always-unplaced baseline of 0.73.
Features such as interviews attended come from the same placement funnel that produces the target label.
These are synthetic holdout metrics and are not real-world accuracy estimates.
